section.heading: Investigatory powers of Attorney General for the District of Columbia.

para.text: In the course of an investigation to determine whether to seek relief under § 28-3909, the Attorney General for the District of Columbia may:
Require sworn answers in writing to written interrogatories; and
Compel production of records, books, papers, contracts, and other documents, verified by a sworn certificate of completion.

Service of any demand document issued under this section may be made by first-class mail, electronic mail, or any other method reasonably calculated to give actual notice; provided, that the Superior Court of the District of Columbia may exercise jurisdiction over the recipient to compel a response consistent with the due process clause of the Constitution of the United States.

Information obtained under this section shall not be admissible in a later criminal proceeding against the person who provides the information or evidence, except with respect to sworn statements that are themselves the basis for a subsequent perjury prosecution.
A subpoena or request for interrogatories issued pursuant to subsection (a) of this section shall be issued in accordance with § 1-301.88d.
